result:
Done — `index.html` is written and verified.

Verification performed (headless, via node, extracting the script and stubbing canvas/rAF):

- **Contract**: `getState()` returns the exact shape; `poly` metadata fixed at `n:9, radius:260, periodSec:7`; `angle` is a pure function of `t` (`2πt/7`, normalized) and matched an independent recomputation to 1e-9 on every sample.
- **Determinism**: `step(5)` ≡ `5 × step(1)` in `t` and `angle`; two fresh loads of the same call sequence produce bit-identical ball state. No `Math.random()` anywhere. `step()` latches manual mode so `requestAnimationFrame` only draws from then on.
- **Invariants over 9000 steps (~75 s simulated, mixed dt of 1/60, 1/120, 1/240)**: all 13 balls satisfied all 9 half-plane constraints with max wall overage `0.000000` px; minimum pairwise distance `28.0000` (strict ≥ 2r); `t` matched the accumulated sum exactly; no NaN. Invariants also hold at `t=0` before any step (all velocities zero, balls clustered within 60 px of the centre).
- **Spin**: ball-ball tangential friction had a torque sign error on one of the two bodies; fixed. A grazing-pair test now gives both balls the same-sign spin (`+1.3957` each), and over 30 s of real simulation peak |ω| reaches ~30.7 rad/s (~41 revolutions), so the drawn numbers visibly rotate.

Physics is hand-written: gravity, exponential air drag, Coulomb-clamped contact friction against the wall's surface velocity `ω×r` at the impact point, restitution 0.82, per-substep relaxation (impulses on the first pass, positional separation after) with the wall projection applied last in every pass so a ball-ball push-out can never eject a ball through an edge.
